key_decisions.decision: Keeps each son’s own vessel, fire/incense sequence and uncommanded offering; foreign-fire ambiguity noted without inventing intoxication.
Preserves two parallel divine declarations within verse paragraph and Aaron’s silence without assigning him agreement or suppressed emotion.
Keeps all names, uncle relationship and relatives for kin-brothers, with sanctuary-front/outside movement.
Retains garments and obeyed removal without claiming bodies or clothes were reduced to ashes.
Preserves named survivors, both mourning restrictions, death and communal wrath, while allowing wider Israel’s mourning and naming LORD as agent.
Keeps location restriction, death risk and anointing reason, then returns to narrator for obedience.
Preserves direct address to Aaron, not mechanically replacing with Moses formula.
Keeps addressees, both drink categories, entering-service context, death consequence and lasting scope without retroactively alleging sons’ drunkenness.
Retains two separate category pairs and keeps sentence connected to teaching duty.
Keeps survivors named, remainder, unleavened preparation, altar-side eating and most-holy category.
Retains clean versus holy place and explicit daughters permitted this food, without broadening earlier most-holy food rule.
Retains emphatic searching, discovery of burning, anger and repeated surviving-son designation.
Preserves Moses’ question, holiness, understood divine giver named for clarity and priests bearing communal guilt without collapsing to personal guilt.
Keeps interior-blood exception’s absence and emphatic should-have-eaten, consistent with 6:30.
Keeps unresolved they, Aaron’s first-person loss and rhetorical question about acceptable eating without adding a settled legal rationale.
Preserves Moses’ favorable response and echo of pleasing in Aaron’s question without inventing a new command or rebuke.
